chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ali, the scribe, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Abdullah ibn Abi Shayba, from Hariz, from Ati'ah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadan, who said:

Two men entrusted a deposit to a trustworthy woman and said to her, 'Do not hand it over to either one of us until we are both gathered at your place.' Then they left and were absent. One of them came to her and said, 'Give me my deposit, for my companion has died.' She refused, and he kept arguing with her until she gave it to him. Then the other one came and said, 'Give me my deposit.' She said, 'Your companion took it, and mentioned that you had died.'

The matter was raised to Umar. Umar said to her, 'I do not see you except as one who is liable (guarantor).' The woman said, 'Make Ali (peace be upon him) the judge between me and him.' Umar said, 'Judge between them.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'This deposit is with me. You both instructed her not to hand it over to either one of you until you are both gathered at her place. So bring me your companion.' Thus he did not hold her liable, and Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'They only intended to take the woman's wealth (by one claiming the other died and taking the whole deposit).'

key_terms.فَلَمْ يُضَمِّنْهَا: He did not hold her liable

ai.seo_question: How did Ali (peace be upon him) rule on the liability of a trustee when one of two depositors claimed the other died?
ai.summary: This narrative, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights Imam Ali’s judicial acumen in resolving a dispute over a conditional deposit (*wadi'ah*) by strictly adhering to the parties' original agreement rather than presuming liability. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise contractual interpretation and the prevention of opportunistic claims, illustrating how Ali (AS) exposed the men's scheme to appropriate the entire sum by leveraging the specific condition of mutual presence.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Ali, the scribe, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Abdullah Bin Abu Shayba, from Hareyz, from Atiya Bin Al Saib, from Zadan who said,

‘Two men entrusted a woman with an entrustment and both said to her, ‘Do not hand it over to anyone one from us until we are gathered in your presence’. Then they both left. So they were both absent (for a time), and then one of the two came to her, so he said, ‘Give me my entrustment, for my companions has died’. But she refused, to the extent that their differing were numerous, then she gave it to him. Then the other one came over, so he said, ‘Give me my entrustment’. So she said, ‘You companions has taken it, and mentioned that you had died’.

So the matter was raised to Umar. So Umar said to her, ‘I do not see you except as one who is responsible’. So the woman said, ‘I make Ali<sup>asws</sup> between me and him’. So Umar said, ‘Judge between the two’. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This (woman) is the entrustment in my<sup>asws</sup> presence, and you had both instructed her that she should not hand it over to any one of you until you are both gathered in her presence. So come to me<sup>asws</sup> with your companion (the other man who took the money)’. Thus he<sup>asws</sup> did not hold her to be responsible, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, they had both intended to go away with the wealth of the woman’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yusuf ibn ‘Aqif from Muhammad ibn Qays who has narrated the following:

“Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that about the case of a man who had a sheep told his people, ‘If you eat all of it, it then is yours; but if you could not eat, then you must pay such and such amount.’ ’
Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, issued a judgment that said, ‘It is invalid. There is nothing in eating food, more or less’; and he (the Imam) prohibited it.”
